chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:

Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: There are four upon whom full prayer may become obligatory, whether they are in travel or in residence: the mukārī, the karī, the shepherd, and the ishtiqān, because it is their work.

key_terms.التَّمَامُ: performing the salat (prayer) in full rather than shortened form
key_terms.الِاشْتِقَانُ: a worker whose occupation involves ongoing movement or travel
key_terms.الْكَرِيُّ: a hired transporter or one engaged in conveyance work
key_terms.الْمُكَارِي: one whose occupation involves transport or hired riding animals
key_terms.سَفَرٍ: travel, as a legal state affecting prayer rulings

ai.seo_question: Who must perform full salat (prayer) while traveling according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling about certain people whose occupation is bound up with continual movement or travel. For such individuals, the obligation is to perform salat (prayer) in full, because travel is considered part of their regular work rather than an exceptional state.
